content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":4,"description_fidelity":7,"readability_1x":6,"pixel_craft":5,"palette_discipline":6,"appeal":5},"score":53,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The enlarged body uses an inconsistent outline: the upper-left is black-bordered while the right side ends directly in bright blue, unlike typical MM2/MM3 contour control.","The huge rectangular white face dominates the sprite and makes it read more like a floating mask or owl than a mechanical squid.","The eyes are tiny cyan marks inside heavy black boxes, so their expression and intended red-warning flash would be difficult to read at 1x.","The lower tentacles are uneven, angular bars with awkward gaps; the far-right appendage especially looks detached from the body.","Several staircase contours around the dome and side fins feel mechanically generated rather than deliberately clustered.","Black, white, and multiple blues crowd some tile regions, making the palette less disciplined than a typical Capcom enemy sprite.","The sprite lacks a clear mine-like mechanical cue such as a warning lens, seam, fuse detail, or armored shell segmentation."],"fixes":["Reduce the white face by 2-3 pixels in width and 1 pixel in height, then use the recovered space for a stronger dark shell contour.","Carry a consistent 1-pixel black outline around the right body edge and simplify both side contours into cleaner stepped curves.","Replace each boxed eye with a compact 2x2 or 2x3 eye cluster that can palette-swap cleanly from white or cyan to red.","Attach every tentacle directly to the underside and redesign them as three or four compact tapered limbs with clearly different gathered and thrust animation poses.","Remove the isolated-looking far-right blue bar and merge it into a single outlined tentacle cluster.","Limit each 8x8 region to black plus two body colors and transparency where possible; reserve white for the face and red for the warning frame.","Add one small central warning lens or shell seam to communicate the swimming-mine function without adding noise."]}
